findings.failure_path: Acceptance requires 'both package-lock.json version fields' to be 0.13.0, but the packet exposes only one lockfile and only its first two version keys. Any remaining 0.12.0 in a second lockfile or a nested self-referencing lockfile entry is undetectable here; the tag-vs-package.json gate in npm-publish.yml compares only package.json, so a stale lockfile version publishes silently.
findings.smallest_fix: Include in the candidate a repo-wide grep receipt showing zero remaining 0.12.0 version strings across all package.json/package-lock.json files, or add that check to the publish workflow.

findings.failure_path: Base binding is a bare unsigned text line written by the implementer, consumed by no gate or script. The reviewer cannot distinguish it from a fabricated or stale SHA, and dev can advance after it is written, so the 'minimal change against origin/dev' claim is self-adjudicated with no upstream trigger.
findings.smallest_fix: Have the review gate recompute git ls-remote refs/heads/dev at review time and fail when it differs from the attested SHA, instead of trusting the committed file.

findings.failure_path: Semver classification as a minor bump rests entirely on out-of-packet prose (semver-comparison evidence). Nothing in the landing-bound diff records the compared range or asserts no public entrypoint removal, so a breaking delta already on dev would ship as 0.13.0 with no gate firing.
findings.smallest_fix: Commit the git diff --name-status ccl-skills-v0.12.0..<attested dev SHA> output as evidence alongside the base attestation.

findings.failure_path: Rollback readiness is claimed via docs/npm-release.md's deprecate-and-fix-forward section, which is not in the diff and imposes no executable precondition. Once 0.13.0 is published, the only recovery is a manual npm deprecate that no gate verifies is reachable (token scope, protected environment access).
findings.smallest_fix: Record in the release evidence a named authorized party plus verified deprecate/dist-tag rollback path before the publish step is authorized.

concern_results.conclusion: Falsified on three axes. Version consistency: acceptance asserts 'both package-lock.json version fields' / a second lockfile, but the packet contains exactly one lockfile and only its first two version keys; any other 0.12.0 occurrence (second lockfile, nested self-reference entry) is outside the packet and would ship mismatched metadata. Base binding: the attestation file is an unsigned implementer-written line that no gate parses and nothing re-verifies, so it is self-adjudicated and goes stale as soon as dev advances past f156079. Semver classification and rollback readiness are asserted only in prose evidence; the diff carries no artifact tying 0.13.0 to a minor-level delta and no rollback record. Tag/default-branch enforcement and authorization separation are untouched by the diff, but the publish workflow's tag-vs-package.json check fires only on a tag push this candidate never exercises, so version consistency stays unverified until publish is already authorized.
